title: Felix and the Salt
premise: Vesper Eastwick, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Salt, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Compass, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the crown's witchfinders begin hunting anyone with the gift, Vesper's carefully hidden magic marks her, and she learns the guild itself has been selling its own gifted members to the crown. To survive, she must find the Salt Door, the last passage out of a homeland that was magically erased from maps and memory decades ago, guarded by the ghost of her dead mentor and the found family she's built in the guild's shadows. In the end, Vesper discovers the door can only open for those who surrender their most precious memory, and she must choose between erasing the loyalty that defines her or staying to break the guild's ledger and give the erased country back its name.
about_author: Lior Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime trade records before turning to fiction, a past that haunts every ledger and salt-stained page they write. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write stories about people who keep promises to things that cannot answer.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet her balancing the Gilded Compass's accounts—trades in bottled grief and borrowed luck—while hiding her own gift of reading the true weight of objects. Her god, Salt, has been silent for seven years, and she prays anyway. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Fishmarket
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The crown posts a bounty on the gifted; a young dock boy Vesper quietly protects is seized in broad daylight. She intervenes with a ledger trick that saves him but exposes a flicker of magic to a witchfinder named Corvane, who begins asking questions. Emotional beat: fear arriving like cold water; invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and Tam (the dock boy, now guild errand-runner). Vesper discovers entries in the oldest ledgers showing the guild has been selling gifted members to the crown for decades—including, possibly, her mentor Ash. Emotional beat: the ground tilting; the family that sheltered her may be the trap.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Ghost
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following Ash's marginalia, she seeks a disgraced cartographer who once mapped the country that no longer exists. He is dead, but his ghost remains, bound to an unfinished map, and confirms the Salt Door is real—inside the erased country's borders, which now lie beneath the capital itself. Emotional beat: grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wounds
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Corvane raids the guild's lower floors; Tam hides the ledgers and takes a whipping rather than give up names. Vesper returns to find her found family bleeding and realizes the guildmaster, Odile, tipped off the raid to flush out traitors. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by betrayal; the family fractures.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The ghost reveals the Salt Door's cost: it opens only for one who surrenders their most precious memory to the silent god. Vesper realizes Salt's silence isn't absence—the god has been devouring memories, and her own forgotten past is stored in the ledgers she keeps. Emotional beat: horror and strange kinship with the god.

chapters.title: Ash, Unforgotten
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Reading her own erased history, Vesper learns she was born in the vanished country, and Ash gave her to Salt to save her from the first purge—the silence she prayed through was the shape of her own sacrifice. Odile confronts her, offering safety for the ledgers. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from ash; rage with purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Descent
chapters.summary: Vesper and Tam's POV, alternating. With the cartographer's ghost and two loyal guild smugglers, they descend beneath the capital through flooded archives toward the door, hunted by Corvane and Odile's enforcers. Tam nearly drowns; Vesper uses her gift openly for the first time, reading the weight of a collapsing tunnel to save him. Emotional beat: found family chosen in fire.

chapters.title: Where the Country Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the Salt Door, Odile and Corvane corner them; the ghost of Ash manifests through the door and unmakes Odile's claim on the ledgers. Vesper stands at the threshold, memory in hand, as the door demands its price—and she understands she can give a different memory: the guild's, not hers. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, coda with Tam. Vesper feeds Salt the guild's founding memory, breaking its power over the erased country—borders shimmer back onto maps, and the vanished nation's name returns to every mouth. Salt speaks at last, one word: her name. Vesper stays, not to hide, but to rebuild. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth reconciled; home remade rather than fled.
